newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek police clash at Canadian TVX Gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Greek police clash at Canadian TVX Gold mine.

text.p: Greek riot police clashed on Thursday with local residents blockading the access road to Canada's TVX Gold operations south of this port city, several people were injured and eight arrested, police said.
At least one person was kept in hospital and several others were released after being treated for lighter injuries. Most of those arrested were also released later, they said.
The trouble began when some local residents, trying to stop TVX Gold from setting up a processing plant, threw rocks and sticks at a driver trying to reach the mining site, police said.

Police rushed to the scene then clashed with the protesters. So far the police have not tried to force open the main access road which has been blockaded for 10 months. Local residents say the processing plant will wreck the environment and tourism.
"There are violent clashes ... There are a number of injured and some, including local officials, have been arrested," George Kostis, president of nearby Varvara village, said earlier.
TVX Gold Hellas, the company's Greek subsidiary, threatened on Wednesday to stop work and halt wages for 650 workers at the TVX operation from next week unless the access road was opened.
Local residents of Varvara and nearby Olympiada have blocked the main road since TVX bought the mine last December.
Greece's deputy national police chief, Haralambos Skitsos, is in the area and directing operations. He has been trying to convince the residents to lift their blockade, police said.
TVX paid $47 million for the mines south of Salonika. Greece said the deal represented a $270 million foreign investment -- the largest in 30 years.
After the threat to suspend work by TVX Gold Hellas, Greek Development Minister Vasso Papandreou said the government would ensure the mines could operate normally.

"The government will not give in. The government will honour its signature. It will not give in to the illegal acts of small interest groups which embarrass our country internationally," she said in a statement.
